name: Dink (Cross-court)
summary: The cross-court dink travels diagonally from your kitchen to theirs. It is the safest dink on the court — the diagonal is the longest line available and the net is lowest in the middle — and it is also the one that creates angles. Most dinking rallies above 3.5 are played cross-court by default.
whenToUse: You are settled at the kitchen line and want the highest-margin dink available.
You want to pull one opponent wide and open the middle behind them.
The straight-ahead player is the stronger of the two.
You are setting a trap — a predictable cross-court dink is what an erne feeds on.
howTo: Turn your shoulders toward the diagonal instead of reaching across your body.
Get low and take the ball out in front, below the waist.
Push through the ball with the shoulder and let the longer distance do the work.
Aim just past the net on their side, wide of their sideline foot rather than at the corner.
Recover a step toward the middle, because a good cross-court dink invites one back.
commonMistakes: Reaching across your body without moving your feet, which leaks the ball into the middle.
Aiming for the corner and finding the sideline instead — the angle is already generous without it.
Hitting it deep enough that it lands near their kitchen line and comes back as a speed-up.
Standing still after hitting, so the reply lands in the space you just created for them.
Playing every dink cross-court until the pattern is obvious and somebody ernes it.

drills.name: Cross-court only
drills.description: Two players, diagonally opposite at the kitchen. Every ball must be cross-court. Count consecutive dinks that stay below net height on the way over; a straight-ahead ball ends the count.

drills.name: Widen it
drills.description: Same rally, but each pair of dinks has to land a little wider than the last until somebody misses or the ball leaves the sideline. It teaches you where the real edge of the angle is.

mistake.label: Too deep: it lands near their kitchen line at a height they can attack, and the speed-up comes straight back at you.
